_comment: Species definitions. Base stats and presentation only; a live creature's current HP and energy belong to a creature_instance, never here (TECHNICAL_START.md, Creature Data vs Creature Instance). M11 replaces `model` and the colours with real rigged creatures without touching combat code.
_comment_moves: Each species carries a `moves` field (D30, creature progression): {"quick": id, "charged": id}, both ids into data/moves/moves.json. Chosen for flavour fit, not balance -- every move ships at power 1.0 so this is balance-neutral. Related species (an evolution line, a shared archetype) may reuse the same move id on purpose; see data/moves/moves.json for the full pool.
_placeholder: M2 ships coloured capsules on purpose. CLAUDE.md forbids judging creature appeal on placeholders, so these are shaped for READABILITY at combat distance — clearly different silhouettes and clearly different colours — and nothing else.
_comment_catch: `catch_rate` is the species' base share of the catch formula in scripts/combat/catch_math.gd. Lower is rarer. Every species must declare one; tests/test_catch_math.gd fails the build if any is missing, because a creature that is accidentally trivial to catch is the kind of bug nobody reports.
_comment_names: Ids and display names for the wild roster are canon from `docs/art/wild/` — the owner's Meadows Wild Canon Pack, which supersedes `docs/art/ROSTER_MANIFEST.md` for these creatures (`docs/decisions/D13`). The meshes under them do not all match yet: Tuskroot is still a songbird from the Plumberry pack (`docs/decisions/D10`) and is the last stand-in in the table. Bramblebun WAS a duck and is not any more — it was produced properly from its own sheet.
_comment_scale: Creatures stand as PEERS to the 1.8m trainer, not as pets at his ankles (docs/decisions/D12), and the band was raised a second time by D19 (starters at boar scale) and WIDENED a third time by D69, this pass, on the owner's direction to 'widen the creature band size if appropriate'. The band now runs 0.60-2.60m, a 4.33x span over seventeen species, where D19 left it at 1.35-2.60m and 1.93x. Every metre of that widening comes from the BOTTOM: the starters (1.90-2.00m) and the whole large tier are untouched, because D19's finding was owner-play evidence that the creature you PILOT felt small, and shrinking those would re-break exactly what D19 fixed. Radii scale by the SAME ratio as height per D12, so nothing gets easier to hit relative to its own size and creature_body._fit()'s footprint allowance sees an unchanged ratio. The reference sheets' real-world sizes (Terrapup 0.45m at the shoulder) are the CREATURE'S biology, not its game scale, and the two are allowed to differ -- see D12/D19/D69.
_comment_wild_stats: TUNABLE, all of them. The wild roster's statlines are set from the sheets' own ROLE and STRENGTHS lines and from nothing else: a digger is tougher than a scout, a tracker hits harder than it takes, a shell is defence and a raptor is not. Nobody has played a fight with any of them yet, so treat every number below as a first guess that combat feedback is expected to move.
_comment_wild_heights: Heights follow D13's rule -- the sheets' RELATIVE ordering is preserved -- through every rescale this file has had. D69 widened the band to 0.60-2.15m for the wild roster around starters left at 1.90-2.00m. The ordering is bit-for-bit the same as D19 left it, including the ties D19 itself preserved (Trailpup and Duskhush still tie in the middle). Pipwing and Bramblebun are still the smallest pair; Meadowhart, Galecrest and Tuskroot still the largest wild tier. The pack's own centimetre figures (Pipwing 0.25m body length, Galecrest 1.80m) are the creature's biology, not its game scale, exactly as sheets 01-04's figures already are.
_comment_evolution_size: An evolution is ALWAYS larger than the form it came from -- the owner's rule, `docs/decisions/D17`. Every `evolves_into` target must have a strictly greater `placeholder.height` than its source. This constrains RELATIVE size inside a line only; the absolute band is D12/D13's settled policy as amended by D19 and widened by D69 (0.60-2.60m overall). Mudsnout 0.95m -> Tuskroot 2.15m satisfies it with a great deal more room than it used to: D69 pulled the pre-evolution down without moving the evolved form, so the line now more than doubles in height, which is what an evolution ought to look like. It satisfied D17 by accident until tests/test_evolution_links.gd started failing loudly on it, because heights here are tunable and a tune that inverts a line is otherwise completely silent.
_comment_aggressive: `aggressive` decides whether a wild creature will start a fight on its own. GAME_DESIGN.md 14 forbids simple proximity starting a fight with a PEACEFUL creature, and the same list allows 'Aggressive creature initiates' — so this flag is the line between those two rules, and it lives in data because it is a property of the creature, not of the code.
_comment_best_creature: R4.7, GAME_DESIGN.md 12: 'Best Creature abilities should be species-specific where possible.' `kind` is `survivability` (a percentage bonus to the effective defence a Best Creature fights with) or `energy` (the same percentage bonus applied to energy gained from a landed quick attack) — the two D30-era combat hooks that already exist. Read only through `creature_species.best_creature_ability()`, and only applied when a creature is the party's flagged Best Creature (`autoload/party.gd::best()`); it never affects a creature nobody has designated. Traversal and other perk kinds named by GAME_DESIGN.md 12 are not built — no out-of-exploration companion-speed system exists yet for one to hook into.

placeholder._comment_footprint: How long this body may be for its width, as a multiple of its collider diameter. A quadruped is genuinely several times longer than it is wide; a frog is not. Set too low and creature_body._fit() scales the model DOWN to fit the allowance and the creature renders shorter than its own collider claims — silently, until MA4.
placeholder._comment_art: Rigged and animated. The model is measured and fitted to `height` at load by creature_body._fit(), so the collider — and therefore the hit cone and the catch accuracy bonus — does not move when the art is swapped. `colour` is retained only for the fallback capsule.
placeholder._comment_animations: 26 clips ship baked into each .glb, so nothing is retargeted and nothing can be mangled. `pain` and `fall_over` are what hit and faint have wanted since M2; `uppercut` is a real committed swing rather than a lunge with no animation.
placeholder._comment_size: Chibi bipeds beside a 1.8m trainer, so they read as companions rather than as livestock — which is the Palworld register. Sized against each other so the practice creature is smaller than your partner and the one that ambushes you is bigger than both.
placeholder._comment_pack: Plumberry Plains Vol. 2, and it answers the review's first and largest complaint directly. The critic's words were 'none of them is a designed creature... Palworld's entire proposition is that its creatures are drawn characters — bold silhouette, hue-opposed to the environment, exaggerated proportion, expression', and that the previous roster put 'a naturalistic tree frog, a faceted grey low-poly goat, and a Nintendo Mii in the same 300 pixels'. These are ten designed chibi characters from ONE artist, which fixes the design AND the cohesion complaint at once.
placeholder._comment_pick:
Chosen on MEASURED colour, not taste. The first pick was fox, rabbit and wolf — which turned out to be the three LEAST saturated characters in the pack (0.20, 0.19, 0.15), i.e. exactly the defect the critic named on the creature they replaced: 'saturation 0.12... a grey rock standing on olive ground... your own creature is the least readable object in your own fight'. Re-picked against its stated criterion — hue-opposed to a green world, and readable at 40px:
  bear      hue  23 deg, sat 0.77, val 0.61  — orange-brown, the most saturated thing in the pack
  duck      hue  42 deg, sat 0.67, val 0.95  — bright gold
  songbird  hue 194 deg, sat 0.36, val 0.72  — blue, the only cool hue available
Three hues, three values, none of them the chartreuse the ground is made of.
placeholder._comment_role: Your partner, and therefore the one that must never be lost in a frame — so it gets the most saturated character in the pack.

bramblebun._comment: The practice creature. Peaceful, common, and generous to catch: it is the one the owner will throw at twenty times while deciding whether throwing is fun, and a rare target would make that a test of patience instead.
bramblebun._comment_of19: TUNABLE, nudged 0.55 -> 0.6 for OF19 (owner report: catching an ordinary Meadows creature burned through too much of the 15-orb starting stock). See catch_math.gd + data/config/catching.json's chance block for the rest of the retune; this alone is the species half of it.

placeholder._comment_height_0828: 0.78 -> 0.96. OWNER DIRECTIVE 2026-08-28 section 2b: 'creatures need to stand out in the grass. some are now too small to see... bramble bun might be both.' Measured rather than eyeballed, as that directive asks: data/config/grass_field.json puts a tuft at height_near 0.40 to height_far 0.62 with height_jitter 0.38, so the field stands 0.25-0.86m -- and Bramblebun at 0.78 was SHORTER than its own tall grass. A frame of the real thing at throwing range (shots/catch/01-aiming-full-health.png) measured only 35% of the creature's own bounding box actually showing creature; the other 65% was blades in front of it. 0.96 clears the tallest tuft by 0.10m. Deliberately modest, per CLAUDE.md's 'modest scale' lever: this is the smallest step that puts the whole silhouette above the field rather than a size that would make a rabbit read as a mid-tier creature. NOTE this moves gameplay too, and that is correct -- creature_body.gd's own header says height and radius drive the capsule, the hit cone's reach and (through body_radius()) the catch accuracy bonus, and scaling the art alone is the invisible discrepancy PW2 forbids. TUNABLE.
placeholder._comment_field_rim_0828: OWNER DIRECTIVE 2026-08-28 section 2b, the half scale cannot reach: 'or they're the color of the grass'. Measured on a real render at throwing range in real grass -- where the Bramblebun is visible at all, hue separation against the field is fine (47 degrees, tan against green) but LUMINANCE contrast is 1.15:1, and this repo's vegetation.json quotes a blind critic calling 1.00:1 invisible. Hue discrimination falls off with angular size much faster than value does, so 47 degrees of hue does not rescue it at 7.5m on a 7-inch panel. 0.22 against creature_body.gd's FIELD_RIM_MAX 0.30 and the alpha's own 0.65: enough to outline the silhouette against grass, far enough under the alpha's rim that an alpha's identity tell survives. Rim rather than a brighter albedo because these models are self-lit and an albedo change would be invisible -- creature_body.gd::_apply_alpha_presence() made that call first and its reasoning applies unchanged. TUNABLE.

mudsnout._comment_of19: TUNABLE, nudged 0.5 -> 0.55 for OF19 (owner report: catching an ordinary Meadows creature burned through too much of the 15-orb starting stock). See catch_math.gd + data/config/catching.json's chance block for the rest of the retune.

trailpup._comment: Tracker and flanker. The sheet's strengths are Speed, Tracking, Loyalty, so it is the roster's glass canine: it hits harder than anything else at its size and takes hits worse. Explicitly NOT the Ground starter -- no stone plates anywhere on it, which the canon pack names as a hard distinction.

burrowback._comment: Defender/Excavator per the sheet's own ROLE line, STRENGTHS Defense, Digging, Control. Broad low silhouette built for digging and defense, powerful forelimbs with shovel-like claws, rock nodules for natural armor -- so it carries the roster's highest defence alongside Trailpup's attack lead, not the other way round. Medium size class keeps HP moderate rather than tanky-huge. Non-aggressive: a defender protects territory when approached, it does not hunt. All tunable; nobody has fought one yet.

meadowhart._comment: Rideable/Pathfinder per the sheet's own ROLE line, STRENGTHS Speed, Stamina, Navigation. Friendly nature and a light frame -- it is a mount and traversal upgrade, not a fighter, so it sits at moderate HP for its Large size class with attack and defence both below the roster's combat specialists (Burrowback, Trailpup). All tunable; nobody has fought one yet.
meadowhart._comment_rideable: R6.1/R6.2. Riding is DATA, not a hardcoded species check: `creature_species.rideable()` reads this block and `scripts/world/riding_controller.gd` refuses anything that does not carry one, so R8.5's legendary mount is a second block here rather than a second branch in code. Every number below is TUNABLE. `mount_offset` is metres in the creature's own local frame from the point between its feet (creature_body's origin, see `place_on_ground`) to where the rider is seated -- y is a little under two thirds of the 2.05m height, which is this model's back line, and the small negative z sits the rider behind the shoulders rather than on the neck. `ride_speed_multiplier` multiplies the trainer's own `walk_speed` from data/config/movement.json (5.0), so 2.0 is 10 m/s against a 8.6 m/s sprint -- riding has to beat SPRINTING, not walking, or the spec's promise that it 'dramatically improves revisiting known areas' is a lie. `requires_item` is the tack this particular species needs; `can_carry` false would keep the tuning here while disabling the ride, which is how a species gets tuned before it is unlocked.

tuskroot._comment: The one that comes at you. Tougher and rarer than the Hopper, because being ambushed should be a moment rather than an interruption — and because the first thing anyone does when something charges them is find out whether they can beat it.
tuskroot._comment_evolution: Tuskroot is no longer a base creature you meet in the wild — the owner's Meadows Wild Canon Pack makes it the evolved form of Mudsnout, and the ONLY evolution in the biome (docs/decisions/D13). R4.6 built the evolution SYSTEM (scripts/creatures/evolution.gd, data/config/progression.json's `evolution` block); a caught Mudsnout can now actually become this. The pair's heights (Mudsnout 0.95m -> Tuskroot 2.15m after D69's widening) are held apart by D17 and tests/test_evolution_links.gd: the evolved form must always be the larger one.

paddlenewt._comment: Quick Swimmer/Skirmisher per the sheet's own subtitle and build notes (Water Sheet, docs/art/reference/wild/03_Meadows_Wild_Water_Sheet.png): agile amphibious body, webbed toes for quick bursts, soft fins for balance and display, moist skin, no armor plating. A skirmisher hits fast and often rather than tanking -- so it carries the roster's lowest defence (soft-bodied, small) with attack in the upper-middle band (Ripplet/Trailpup territory) and HP on the low side for its Small-Medium size class. Non-aggressive: the sheet's own design notes call the whole Water roster 'friendly, expressive... calm spirits', and Paddlenewt's listed actions are WATER DASH and PLAYFUL POUNCE, not a hunting behaviour. Common (small pond creature): catch rate near Bramblebun/Mudsnout, not Tuskroot's rare end. All tunable; nobody has fought one yet.

mosshell._comment: Steady Tank/Shelter per the sheet's own subtitle and build notes (Water Sheet, docs/art/reference/wild/03_Meadows_Wild_Water_Sheet.png): low center of gravity, high defense, broad shell with mossy stone plates, strong limbs for lakebed traction, withdraws for protection. A tank explicitly built for defence rather than offence -- so it carries the roster's highest defence so far (ahead of Burrowback's 23) and high HP for a Medium size class, with the lowest attack on the roster since it withdraws rather than fights. Non-aggressive, matching the sheet's own 'friendly... calm spirits' design note for the whole Water roster and its SHELL RETREAT listed behaviour. Catch rate near Burrowback's (a slow, armoured creature, not a common skittish one). All tunable; nobody has fought one yet.

brooktail._comment: Resourceful Diver/Helper per the sheet's own subtitle and build notes (Water Sheet, docs/art/reference/wild/03_Meadows_Wild_Water_Sheet.png): strong swimmer and natural diver, water-repellent fur with dense undercoat, webbed feet for steering and balance, quick/clever/sociable, listed actions DIVING SWIM and GATHER & CARRY -- a support/utility creature, not a fighter. Smallest of the six wild quadrupeds finished so far (1.45m), so HP and defence sit at the low end; attack modest but not the lowest, since 'quick and clever' implies some bite. Non-aggressive, matching the sheet's own 'sociable' framing and its Water-roster-wide 'friendly... calm spirits' design note. All tunable; nobody has fought one yet.

placeholder._comment_art: R0.6: tools/art_pipeline finish.py clean -> texture -> rig -> grade -> install, from the R0.4 winner (candidate a). See docs/art/MEADOWS_WILD_PRODUCTION_REPORT.md. TWO known defects on this creature, both flagged rather than fixed: (1) R0.4 recorded a HARD FAIL shared by every candidate -- the canon's broad flat scaled paddle tail is absent, both candidates give a round tapering tail instead. The report's own instruction is to ship it forward with the defect flagged rather than block or re-roll ('iterating on what exists'), and that a real sculpting pass is separate future work -- not attempted here. (2) rig_quadruped.py's automatic weighting left 35 of 14,034 vertices (0.25%) unweighted, the first species in this batch where residual post-retexture mesh noise (6,075 non-manifold edges, 81 microscopic disconnected components -- the same category every species carries after Meshy's retexture re-unwrap, see Tuskroot's DONE.md entry) actually crossed into un-rigged vertices rather than being silently absorbed. Confirmed scattered across the whole body rather than concentrated at the tail, so not obviously the same root cause as (1); will read as tiny pinned-in-bind-pose specks during animation rather than one visible tear. A proper fix likely needs a fresh clean/remesh pass or the eventual tail sculpt, not attempted here. The model is measured and fitted to `height` at load by creature_body._fit(), so the collider -- and therefore the hit cone and the catch accuracy bonus -- does not move when the art is swapped. `colour` is retained only for the fallback capsule.

galecrest._comment: Sky Soarer/Aerial Striker per the Air Sheet (docs/art/reference/wild/04_Meadows_Wild_Air_Sheet.png): medium-large raptor, powerful wings and hooked beak, 'built for speed, lift, and precise control in strong winds' -- a genuine predator, and D13 explicitly requires it not read like the Air starter Galewisp ('not a starter-like cute fox-bird hybrid'). Highest attack of the wild roster so far and the lowest defence, mirroring Galewisp's own thin-armour/high-attack air profile but pushed further since this one is built to strike, not glide. Marked aggressive, unlike the rest of the wild roster bar Tuskroot -- the sheet's own language ('fierce focused eyes', 'Aerial Striker') reads as a real predator rather than a skittish prey animal. First bird species: first exercise of R0.6's rig --kind bird path (rig_bird.py), see the placeholder art comment below.

Two glossy black hooked-beak shapes were checked and rejected as eye_guard candidates in grade.py -- see that file's comment. The model is measured and fitted to `height` at load by creature_body._fit(), so the collider -- and therefore the hit cone and the catch accuracy bonus -- does not move when the art is swapped. `colour` is retained only for the fallback capsule.

duskhush._comment: Silent Watcher/Night Scout per the Air Sheet (docs/art/reference/wild/04_Meadows_Wild_Air_Sheet.png): a small owl built for stealth and observation, not confrontation -- broad silent wings for stealth flight, large eyes for night vision, 'calm watchful' brief (R0.4 production report). Defence and HP sit closer together than Galecrest's spread, reflecting a creature that avoids fights rather than winning them outright; attack is the lowest of the wild roster's air types so far. Catch rate moderate -- a scout is wary, not rare.

pipwing._comment: Zippy Flier/Spotter per the Air Sheet (docs/art/reference/wild/04_Meadows_Wild_Air_Sheet.png): 'tiny and round with oversized eyes for high readability, built for quick bursts of speed and sharp awareness'. Smallest and lightest creature in the roster (docs/art/wild's own roster canon: 'much smaller/lighter than Galecrest', grouped with Bramblebun as the two smallest). Lowest HP and defence of the wild roster so far -- a fragile scout, not a fighter -- but not the lowest attack, since 'quick bursts of speed' implies a real if glancing strike. veridian._comment_type: Board 06 labels it Grass/Earth. The Meadows has three types — Ground, Water, Air — and REFERENCE_CANON's precedence rule is that the markdown wins on type while the image wins on looks, so it is the GROUND legendary per GAME_DESIGN.md section 26.
veridian._comment_catch: The lowest in the game by a wide margin. A legendary you catch on the second orb is not a legendary. TUNABLE.
veridian._comment_rideable: R8.5, and deliberately the SECOND block of exactly the same shape Meadowhart's is (see its own `_comment_rideable` for what every key means) rather than a parallel system: `creature_species.rideable()` and `scripts/world/riding_controller.gd` are untouched by a new mount except for the one key added below. The tier above Meadowhart is THREE things, and only the first is a number. FASTER: 2.8 x the trainer's 5.0 m/s walk = 14 m/s, against Meadowhart's 10 and a sprint's 8.6. NO TACK: `requires_item` is EMPTY, the only mount in the game that needs none. Meadowhart is a saddled animal and the saddle is the permission; this one carries you because it offered to (spec sec28: the legendary voluntarily joins), and strapping the crafting bench's leather to it would be the wrong sentence about what just happened in that chamber. Costs no new code -- riding_controller._has_tack() already returns true for an empty requirement, which is why that key was written per-species in R6.2. AND GROUND NOTHING ELSE HOLDS: `climb_max_slope_deg` becomes the mount's own `floor_max_angle` while it is ridden. MEASURED, not assumed -- scenes/creature.tscn gives EVERY creature 0.9599 rad (55 degrees) and scenes/player.tscn gives the trainer 0.7854 (45), so 55 is the baseline this has to beat, not 45. At 60 the legendary holds flanks that slide every other creature in the roster, including Meadowhart, straight back down. 60 IS A CEILING WITH A REASON: every severed spoke's carve walls are 65-66 degrees (16/7, 11/5 and 9/4 in terrain_playground.json's own carves), so this mount still cannot climb out of a rift trench and D23's carve-out survives it -- tests/smoke_boss.gd drives a probe body at this exact limit at the storm-road seam to prove it, and tests/smoke_riding.gd fails the build if the number is ever raised into that band. TUNABLE below that line only.
